newsitem.title: UK: BA prepares to bid for France's Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: BA prepares to bid for France's Air Liberte.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Monday it hopes to lodge a bid for troubled French regional carrier Air Liberte with a Paris court before 1400 GMT today, the deadline set for bids by its administrators.
"We are working towards submitting a bid but there are still a number of issues that need to be resolved," a spokesman said.
"We will not be able to confirm whether or not we have bid until later today."
British Airways has said it believes it can revive Air Liberte by merging it with its own French subsidiary TAT.

Earlier this month it asked the European Commission to block any bid made for Liberte by another French carrier AOM, alleging that an AOM bid would be tantamount to a state subsidised rescue for the airline.
AOM is also up for sale as a condition of state aid granted to its parent, the state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais.

BA said in letters sent last month to European commissioners for transport and competition Neil Kinnock and Karel van Miert that a takeover of Liberte by AOM would add to the liabilities facing AOM, thereby contravening the conditions of the Credit Lyonnais aid.
AOM is owned by the Consortium de Realisation, the holding company charged with selling Credit Lyonnais assets under the state-supported rescue plan.
BA says it fears the French government wants French interests to take over Liberte to prevent BA or any other foreign airline getting hold of more runway slots at Paris' short haul airport at Orly.
It said it had noted French press reports at the end of September saying the authorities had already approved a so-called "French solution" that would swallow up Air Liberte.

Le Monde had said Paris wanted to see the creation of a second domestic force to Air France, built around a new French airline based on a fusion of AOM, Air Liberte and the privately-owned carrier Euralair.

Instead BA says it believes it can turn Air Liberte around although it is currently in poor shape, noting that the airline lost 650 million francs in the first nine months of this year and has total debts of about 1.5 billion francs.
Liberte has begun a recovery plan that involves taking several large planes out of its fleet and cutting routes -- both long-haul to Africa and Canada and some internal ones.
The plan, under which it is cutting 285 jobs and focusing on medium- and short-haul flights, is to run for about six months.
Several other airlines and travel companies have said they could be interested in taking over Liberte since it was placed under bankruptcy protection by a Paris court on September 26.
British entrepreneur Richard Branson said last week his Virgin Express European short-haul airline might bid against his arch rival British Airways for Air Liberte.
No one at the company was immediately available on Monday to confirm whether Virgin was going ahead with a bid today.
